<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6. Allowance for Doubtful
Accounts and Notes Receivable</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
activity in the allowance for doubtful accounts and notes receivable is as
follows (in thousands):</font></p>

<table border="1" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border:none;border-collapse:collapse;margin-left:20.0pt;">

  <td width="205" valign="bottom" style="border:none;padding:0pt .7pt 0pt 0pt;width:153.4pt;">

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9. Business Combinations</font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2004 Acquisitions</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;15, 2004, the Company acquired 100% of
the membership interests of KeyPoint Consulting&nbsp;LLC (&#147;KeyPoint&#148;), located
in Emeryville and Los Angeles, California. KeyPoint is an economic consulting
firm with approximately 26 principals and staff, and a network of academic
affiliates. KeyPoint provides economic, financial, and forensic accounting
services in matters involving complex litigation and regulation. KeyPoint&#146;s
clients include companies, law firms, and government and regulatory agencies. The
acquisition of KeyPoint significantly expands the Company&#146;s expertise in new
practice areas and helps strategically position the Company for additional
growth in its legal consulting area reported in the Healthcare, Regulatory, and
Legal Compliance segment. Key Point contributed $5.6 million in revenue in
2004, or approximately 2.9% of total segment revenue, and was moderately
accretive to 2004 earnings after consideration of related financing costs and
amortization of identified intangibles.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
aggregate consideration paid during the second quarter for KeyPoint consisted
of $13.7&nbsp;million in cash. An additional $1.5 million in cash was paid
during the third quarter, in accordance with the acquisition agreement. The
allocation of the purchase price is set forth below (in thousands):</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SOURCECORP, INCORPORATED AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">9.

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$1.9 million was assigned
to non-compete agreements with a useful life of four&nbsp;years. The remaining
goodwill of $12.0&nbsp;million will be tested annually for impairment. Approximately
$4.6 million of the goodwill is deductible for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">2002 Acquisitions</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective
January&nbsp;1, 2002, the Company acquired 100% of the outstanding shares of
United Information Services,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;UIS&#148;), located in Iowa, and expanded
the Company&#146;s statement processing service offering within the Information
Management and Distribution segment, which had existing locations in Arizona
and New York. The aggregate consideration paid for UIS consisted of
$17.2&nbsp;million in cash. Also, the former shareholders of UIS are eligible
to receive up to an additional $10.0&nbsp;million in the Company&#146;s common stock
and cash if there is no breach in representations and warranties of the
acquisition agreement, and certain future revenue, earnings and cash flow
targets are achieved over the three year period ended December&nbsp;31, 2004.
The allocation of the purchase price is set forth below (in thousands):</font></p>

 <tr bgcolor="#CCEEFF">
  <td width="487" valign="top" style="padding:0pt .7pt 0pt 0pt;width:365.35pt;">
  <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Consideration
  paid</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the $16.2&nbsp;million of goodwill and other
intangibles recorded from the acquisition, $4.0&nbsp;million was assigned to
customer relationships with a useful life of 15&nbsp;years and approximately
$0.4&nbsp;million was assigned to non-compete agreements with a useful life of
5&nbsp;years. The remaining goodwill of $11.7&nbsp;million is tested annually
for impairment and is not deductible for tax purposes.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2004,
all of the $10.0 million of additional consideration has been recorded as
additional goodwill related to this acquisition in accordance with the
acquisition agreement.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div>
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SOURCECORP, INCORPORATED AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9. Business
Combinations (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At October&nbsp;31, 2004, the Company performed the
annual goodwill impairment test as required by SFAS No.&nbsp;142. The Company
compared the fair values of the reporting units to their carrying values. In
determining the fair value of the reporting units, the Company used the Income
Approach and the Market Approach. The fair value of all reporting units
exceeded their carrying value at October&nbsp;31, 2004. As such, no impairment
for goodwill was recognized.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2004, net aggregate goodwill
deductible for tax purposes was approximately $151.5&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Due to the fact that the Company is primarily a
services company, its business acquisitions typically result in significant
amounts of goodwill and other intangibles. Therefore, an impairment charge
resulting from goodwill and other intangibles could result in a material
adverse impact on the Company&#146;s financial statements during the period
incurred.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Contingent
Consideration</font></i></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain of the Company&#146;s acquisitions are subject to
adjustments in overall consideration and recorded goodwill based upon the
achievement of specified revenue and/or earnings targets generally over one to
three year periods. In certain agreements, the Company reserves the right to
change the payment mix to use common stock versus cash in satisfying contingent
consideration liabilities. In transactions where the Company acquired a
subsidiary through a tax-free stock merger, the Company is required to pay a
minimum amount of total consideration in common stock rather than cash,
including any contingent consideration payments.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management&#146;s evaluation of the cumulative earnings of
acquired companies through December&nbsp;31, 2004 indicated that certain
acquired companies have met specified earnings targets beyond a reasonable
doubt; therefore the Company accrued aggregate additional consideration of
approximately $5.8 million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004. As of December&nbsp;31,
2004, in connection with the 2002 purchase of UIS, approximately $5.3 million
of additional consideration remains accrued which is classified as other
current liabilities and is expected to be settled in cash during 2005. In
accordance with the agreements, the Company has the option to satisfy the
entire $5.3 million (or any part thereof) in common stock with final valuation
determined at date of issuance.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2004, all periods applicable
for earnout targets of past acquisitions are completed.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Acquisition Related
Receipts/Payments</font></i></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company made net acquisition related payments of $3.0&nbsp;million
in cash during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003 and released 20,268 shares
of common stock from escrow at a price of $13.96 per share at March&nbsp;31,
2003. In addition, the Company received reimbursements of approximately
$1.1&nbsp;million of purchase price related to a past acquisition unrelated to
the Company&#146;s restatement, more fully discussed, in Note 3, recorded as a
reduction to goodwill, in the Information Management and Distribution segment
and made other acquisition related payments of approximately $0.3&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, the
Company paid net consideration of approximately $3.4 million in cash and 30,324
shares of common stock at an average price of $26.12 per share related to
contingent consideration agreements of past acquisitions. Additionally, the
Company paid $13.7 million, net of cash acquired, related to the KeyPoint
acquisition and the associated transaction costs and $0.3 of additional
purchase proceeds related to the purchase agreement of a past acquisition.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In April&nbsp;2001, the Company entered into a line of
credit with a group of banks led by Bank of America, SunTrust Bank and Wells
Fargo Bank, as co-agents (the &#147;2001 Credit Agreement&#148;) and terminated the
previous line of credit agreement. At December&nbsp;31, 2004, under the 2001
Credit Agreement, the Company may borrow on a revolving credit basis loans in
an aggregate outstanding principal amount up to $290.0&nbsp;million, subject to
certain financial covenants and ratios. Through April&nbsp;1, 2006, the 2001
Credit Agreement is secured by the stock of the Company&#146;s material
subsidiaries, and in the event the Company exceeds a designated leverage ratio,
by the assets of the Company and subsidiaries.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31,

million and is scheduled to mature as follows (in millions):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The annual interest rate applicable to borrowings
under this facility is, at the Company&#146;s option, (i)&nbsp;grid pricing ranging
from 0.0% to 0.5% plus the prime rate based on the ratio of funded debt to
earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (&#147;EBITDA&#148;) (as
defined in the credit agreement) or (ii)&nbsp;grid pricing ranging from 1.125%
to 2.0% plus LIBOR based on the ratio of funded debt to EBITDA. The 2001 Credit
Agreement requires mandatory prepayments in certain circumstances, </font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SOURCECORP, INCORPORATED AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">10.
Long-term Obligations and Credit Facilities</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">such as asset
dispositions. The outstanding principal balance of revolving credit loans is
due and payable on April&nbsp;1, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2004, the Company has outstanding
irrevocable letters of credit totaling approximately $12.3&nbsp;million. Letters
of credit in the amount of approximately $8.0&nbsp;million serves as security
for the Company&#146;s self-insured workmen&#146;s compensation program. A letter of
credit in the amount of $2.5&nbsp;million serves as a guarantee for performance
under a contract with New York State Workers Compensation Board. A letter of
credit in the amount of approximately $1.8&nbsp;million serves as guarantee for
periodic principal and interest payments related to the Industrial Revenue
Bonds.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The weighted average interest rate on long-term
obligations during 2003 and 2004 was 4.2% and 3.7%, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2001 Credit Agreement contains certain reporting
requirements and financial covenants, including requirements that the Company
maintain minimum levels of net worth, a maximum ratio of funded debt to EBITDA
and other financial ratios, and prohibits the payment of cash and similar
dividends. These ratios were scheduled to become more restrictive beginning in
the quarter ended December&nbsp;31, 2002 with the leverage ratio declining from
3.0 times to 2.5 times and the fixed charge coverage ratio increasing from 1.25
times to 1.50 times. However, in September&nbsp;2002, an amendment was approved
that extended the fixed cost coverage ratio requirement of 1.25 until January&nbsp;1,
2004 and will increase to 1.35 at all times thereafter. In addition to the
leverage and fixed cost coverage ratios, the Company is subject to minimum net
worth requirements. Effective March&nbsp;26, 2003, an amendment was approved
that allows for the reduction to the minimum net worth requirement for up to
$30&nbsp;million of share repurchases. In addition, effective July&nbsp;30,
2004, an amendment was approved that allows for the reduction to the minimum
net worth requirement for an additional $30 million of share repurchases.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of the Company&#146;s internal investigation,
more fully described in Note 3 to these consolidated financial statements, the
Company was unable to file its September&nbsp;30, 2004 Quarterly Report on Form&nbsp;10-Q
within the timeframe prescribed by the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The
failure to timely file the September&nbsp;30, 2004 Quarterly Report on Form&nbsp;10-Q
resulted in a default under the 2001 Credit Agreement. The Company entered into
a waiver agreement on November&nbsp;12, 2004 with the lenders party to the 2001
Credit Agreement. Pursuant to the terms of the waiver agreement, the lenders
agreed, among other things, to waive any default under the 2001 Credit
Agreement that resulted from potential non-compliance with a designated fixed
charge coverage ratio, and our failure to timely file our Quarterly Report on Form&nbsp;10-Q
for the September&nbsp;30, 2004 quarter. The waiver agreement also provides
that during the period that the waiver agreement is in effect, the outstanding
principal amount of the loans under the 2001 Credit Agreement may not exceed
$112,000,000. The waiver agreement was to expire on March&nbsp;15,
2005;&nbsp;however, on March&nbsp;15, 2005, the Company entered into on Extension
and Modification of Waiver to Credit Agreement, which extended such waiver
through March&nbsp;23, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective March&nbsp;23, 2005, the Company entered
into an amendment to the 2001 Credit Agreement that allows for the exclusion of
certain contingent consideration overpayments to the former owners of the
Operating Subsidiary, as described more fully in Note 3 to these consolidated
financial statements, from the definition of EBITDA. Pursuant to the terms of
the Company&#146;s 2001 Credit Agreement, EBITDA is used in calculating certain
leverage and fixed cost coverage ratios. By not having the March&nbsp;23, 2005
amendment in place, the Company was in a default under the 2001 Credit
Agreement due to the Company </font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10.

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">exceeding the allowable
leverage ratio of 2.5 times for the quarters ended June&nbsp;30, 2004 and September&nbsp;30,
2004, as a result of the contingent consideration overpayments, previously
discussed. As a result, the Company classified the debt under such Credit
Agreement as a Current Maturity included in the current liability section of
its balance sheet at June&nbsp;30 and September&nbsp;30, 2004. Upon entering
the March&nbsp;23, 2005 amendment, the Company cured the default under the 2001
Credit Agreement, as such, reclassifying debt under the Credit Agreement as
Long-Term Obligations. Because the maturity date of the debt under the 2001
Credit Agreement is April&nbsp;1, 2006, unless the maturity date of such debt
is subsequently modified, such debt will be classified to Current Maturity on
and after April&nbsp;1, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December 31, 2004 and through March 31, 2005,
the Company is in compliance with loan covenants after giving effect to the
amendments and waivers described above, which among other things provided for
an amended definition of EBITDA. As of December&nbsp;31, 2004, the availability
under the 2001 Credit Agreement was $8.7&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2000, in
order to mitigate interest rate risk related to the line of credit, the Company
entered into an interest rate hedge agreement in the amount of
$50.0&nbsp;million, whereby the Company effectively fixed the interest rate
through March&nbsp;2003 on the amount of the hedge agreement at 5.775%. The
interest rate hedge agreement expired on March&nbsp;31, 2003 and was not
replaced. See Note&nbsp;14, Interest Rate Swap, regarding the interest rate
hedge.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12. Income Taxes</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a13_stockholdersEquity_122738"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13. Stockholders&#146; Equity</font></b></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock-Based
Compensation:</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2002, the Board of Directors and Shareholders of
the Company approved the 2002 Long-Term Incentive Plan (the &#147;2002 Plan&#148;), which
is described below. The 2002 Plan replaced the 1995 Stock Option Plan, as
amended (the &#147;1995 Plan&#148;). Grants outstanding under the 1995 Plan will continue
to be subject to the provisions of the 1995 Plan; no additional awards will be
granted under the 1995 Plan.</font></p>

<div>
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SOURCECORP, INCORPORATED AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a13_stockholdersEquity_122738"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13. Stockholders&#146; Equity</font></b></a>
(Continued)</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2002 Plan authorizes awards of options to purchase
common stock and may include incentive stock options (&#147;ISOs&#148;) and/or
non-qualified stock options (&#147;NQSOs&#148;), stock appreciation rights, restricted
stock, deferred stock, bonus stock and awards in lieu of cash obligations,
dividend equivalents and other stock-based awards. In addition, the
Company issued warrants (the &#147;Warrants&#148;) to certain key employees and employees
of its subsidiaries. The Company refers to awards under the 2002 Plan and the
1995 Plan collectively as &#147;Awards&#148; and refers to warrants granted from time to
time as Warrants.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors has appointed a committee (the &#147;Committee&#148;),
which is composed of independent, non-employee directors, to administer the
2002 Plan. Persons eligible to receive awards under the plan include directors,
officers and employees of the Company and its subsidiaries, and persons who
provide consulting services to the Company deemed by the Committee to be of
substantial value to the Company, persons who have been offered employment by
the Company or its subsidiaries, and persons employed by an entity that the
Committee reasonably expects to become a subsidiary of the Company. Awards
granted under the plan may, at the discretion of the Committee, be granted
either alone or in addition to, in tandem with or in substitution for any other
award granted under the Plan or any other plan of the Company, any subsidiary
or any business entity to be acquired by the Company or one of its
subsidiaries. The Committee determines vesting in awards granted under the
plan. Historically, when the Company has issued Warrants, it has been either at
the recommendation of the Compensation Committee or the full Board. Each of the
1995 Plan, the 2002 Plan and individual grants of Warrants have been previously
approved by the Company&#146;s stockholders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The total number of shares of common stock that may be
subject to outstanding awards shall not exceed 16% of the total number of
shares of common stock outstanding at the effective time of such grant (or
650,000, whichever is greater), plus an additional 600,000 shares. The number
of shares of common stock that may be issued upon the exercise of ISOs cannot
exceed 650,000. To date, the Company has not issued any <font style="text-transform:uppercase;">iso</font>s. In addition, during any calendar year, no participant
may be granted awards that may be settled by delivery of more than 500,000
shares of common stock, or, in the case of awards that may be settled in cash,
by payment of cash that exceeds the fair market value of 500,000 shares of
common stock, determined either at the time of grant or at the time of payment,
whichever is greater.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2003, the Company awarded 164,300 shares of
restricted stock under the 2002 Plan. The restricted shares were issued at no
cost to the recipients; therefore, the Company recorded deferred compensation
of approximately $2.9&nbsp;million based on the market value of the stock at
the date of issuance. Subsequent to the grant date, certain forfeitures of
restricted stock occurred resulting in a total award of 155,000 shares and
total deferred compensation of $2.8 million. The deferred compensation charge
is being amortized to expense over the vesting period of the restricted stock.
The restricted shares vest over a three-year period ending July&nbsp;1, 2006,
with acceleration of the vesting period occurring if a certain stock price or
performance target is achieved. For the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31,
2003 and 2004, approximately $0.6&nbsp;million and $0.9 million, respectively,
of deferred compensation was amortized to expense related to the 2003 grants of
restricted stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2004, the Company awarded 182,550 shares of
restricted stock under the 2002 Plan. The restricted shares were issued at no
cost to the recipients; therefore, the Company recorded deferred compensation
of approximately $4.6 million based on the market value of the stock at the
date of issuance. Subsequent to the grant date, certain forfeitures of
restricted stock occurred resulting in a total award of&nbsp;177,300 shares and
total deferred compensation of $4.5 million. The deferred compensation charge
is </font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Common Stock
Repurchase Program</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2003, the Company activated the
$30.0&nbsp;million stock repurchase program authorized by the Board of
Directors in April&nbsp;2001 and purchased 1,306,979 shares of its common stock
at a cost of approximately $20.7&nbsp;million. During the second quarter of
2004, the Company purchased an additional&nbsp;361,415 shares of its common
stock at a cost of approximately $9.3 million completing the authorized repurchase
program. The repurchased shares were recorded in the accompanying balance sheet
as a reduction in common stock for the par value of the shares, in additional
paid-in-capital in the amount of $20.0&nbsp;million and in retained earnings in
the amount of $10.0&nbsp;million. These shares were retired and returned to the
status of authorized but unissued shares of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the third quarter
of 2004, the Board of Directors authorized the purchase of an additional&nbsp;$20.0
million of shares from time to time on the open market as conditions warrant. During
the third and fourth quarters of 2004, the Company purchased 117,524 shares of
its common stock at a cost of approximately $2.6 million. The repurchased
shares were recorded in the accompanying balance sheet as a reduction in common
stock for the par value of the shares, in additional paid-in-capital in the
amount of&nbsp;$1.5 million and in retained earnings in the amount of $1.1
million. These shares were retired and returned to the status of authorized but
unissued shares of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net Income (Loss)
Per Share</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic
and diluted net income per share were computed in accordance with SFAS No.&nbsp;128,
<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Earnings Per Share</font></i>. The
differences between basic weighted average common shares and diluted weighted
average common shares and potentially dilutive common shares are as follows (in
thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13. Stockholders&#146; Equity (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2002,
2003 and 2004 approximately 3,579,000, 2,569,000 and 2,997,000 respectively, of
common shares were not included in the diluted earnings per share calculation
because they were anti-dilutive. These common shares may be dilutive in
future earnings per share calculations.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a14_InterestRateSwap_124410"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14. Interest Rate Swap</font></b></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;22, 2000,
the Company entered into an interest rate swap to hedge, through March&nbsp;31,
2003, its exposure to fluctuations in interest rates on $50&nbsp;million of its
debt. This interest rate swap had the effect of fixing the interest rate on
$50&nbsp;million of the Company&#146;s debt at 5.775%. In accordance with SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;133,
the Company concluded the interest rate swap qualified as a cash flow hedge.
The hedge expired on March&nbsp;31, 2003 and was not replaced.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a15_EmployeeBenefitPlans_124413"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15. Employee Benefit Plans</font></b></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains a defined contribution plan (the
&#147;401(k)&nbsp;plan&#148;) that covers the Company&#146;s employees and the employees of
the majority of its subsidiaries. The employees must be at least 21&nbsp;years
of age and are eligible for the plan on the first of the month following
90&nbsp;days of service. The Company also maintains a non-qualified plan (&#147;Rabbi
Trust&#148;) that permits eligible officers and certain highly compensated employees
to defer a portion of their compensation. Contributions to both the 401(k)&nbsp;plan
and the non-qualified compensation plan consist of employee pre-tax
contributions determined as a percentage of each participating employee&#146;s
compensation. The Company may make contributions to either or both plans at the
discretion of the Board of Directors. The Company incurred costs of $0.3 million
and a reduction to expense of $0.3&nbsp;million related to the 401(k)&nbsp;plan
for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2002 and 2003, respectively. No costs
were incurred related to the 401(k)&nbsp;plan fur the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2004. The Company incurred costs of $0.2&nbsp;million, $0.1&nbsp;million and
$0.3&nbsp;million related to the non-qualified compensation plan for the years
ended December&nbsp;31, 2002, 2003 and 2004, respectively. The total value of
the Rabbi Trust at December&nbsp;31, 2004 was approximately $8.9&nbsp;million
and was included in the Company&#146;s consolidated balance sheet as Other
Noncurrent Assets with a corresponding balance in Other Long-Term Obligations.
The Company offers no post-employment or post-retirement benefits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain of the operating
companies have separate qualified defined contribution employee benefit plans
(the &#147;Plans&#148;), the majority of which allow for voluntary pre-tax contributions
by employees. The subsidiaries pay all general and administrative expenses of
the Plans and, in some cases, the subsidiaries make matching and discretionary
contributions to the Plans. The subsidiaries offer no post-employment or
post-retirement benefits. The expense incurred related to the Plans was
approximately $0.1 million in each of the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2002,
2003 and 2004.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a16_RelatedPartyTransactions_124206"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16. Related Party Transactions</font></b></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Leasing
Transactions</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain operating
companies lease their operating facilities from selling parties who remained as
employees. These leases are for various lengths and annual amounts. The rental
expense for these operating leases for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2002,
2003 and 2004 was approximately $1.6 million, $1.6 million and $1.2 million,
respectively. None of these arrangements are with any of the Company&#146;s
directors or executive officers.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a17_CommitmentsAndContingencies_124212"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">17. Commitments and Contingencies</font></b></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Litigation</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is, from time
to time, a party to litigation arising in the normal course of business. The
following is a description of the most significant legal matters that the
Company is involved in. In the event of an adverse outcome in one or more of
the legal proceedings our business, financial condition, results of operations
or cash flows could be materially adversely affected.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Putative Securities
Class&nbsp;Action</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company, and the
Company&#146;s CEO and CFO individually, have been named as defendants in several
putative securities class actions, in response to the Company&#146;s press releases
dated October&nbsp;27,&nbsp;2004, in which the Company disclosed that its
financial statements for certain prior periods should no longer be relied upon,
and also provided updated financial guidance. The complaints (collectively, the
&#147;Actions&#148;) were filed in the United States District Court for the Northern
District of Texas, Dallas Division. The Actions are putative shareholder class
action lawsuits alleging violations of Federal Securities Laws, including
alleged violations of Sections 10(b)&nbsp;and 20(a), and Rule&nbsp;10b-5
of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. The Actions are purportedly
on behalf of all persons who purchased the Company&#146;s common stock during the
period between May&nbsp;7, 2003, and October&nbsp;26, 2004 or October&nbsp;27,
2004, depending on the Action, and seek unspecified damages. The four Actions
have been transferred to a single judge in the Northern District of Texas,
Dallas Division and these actions have been consolidated and a motion is
pending to consolidate each of the actions into a single action styled <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Richard Bassin&nbsp;v. Sourcecorp, Inc., et al</font></i>.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purported
Derivative Action and Demand Letter</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A purported stockholder
derivative action was filed on December&nbsp;28, 2004, against certain of the
Company&#146;s current and former officers and directors as individual defendants
and the Company as a nominal defendant in the 116th District Court for Dallas
County, Texas (the &#147;Purported Derivative Action&#148;). The Purported Derivative
Action alleges breach of fiduciary duty, abuse of control, gross mismanagement,
waste of assets, and unjust enrichment related to the Company&#146;s press release
dated October&nbsp;27, 2004, in which the Company disclosed that its financial
statements for certain prior periods should no longer be relied upon. All of
these claims are asserted derivatively on behalf of the Company. Further, the
Chairman of the Company&#146;s Board of Directors received from a purported
shareholder a demand letter (the &#147;Demand Letter&#148;) based on the same set of
facts as the Purported Derivative Action. The Company has formed a special
committee of the Board of Directors to evaluate the claims made in the
Purported Derivative Action and the Demand Letter.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Digital Imaging
Systems</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;5, 2004,
Digital Imaging Systems,&nbsp;Inc. filed suit against the Company in the United
States District Court-Southern District of New York alleging, among other
things, that a portion of the Company&#146;s process for scanning and indexing
images violates one of Digital Imaging Systems&#146; patents. The Company has
tendered this matter to one of its software/hardware vendors for
indemnification, which such vendor is evaluating. The suit demands unspecified
damages.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">17.
Commitments and Contingencies</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Various ROI Copy
Charge Matters</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, various
subsidiaries of the Company that perform release of information (&#147;ROI&#148;)
services become defendants to putative class action lawsuits generally alleging
that the charge for reproducing certain medical records is not in conformity
with such plaintiffs&#146; reading of the applicable regulated charge. Such suits
typically include multiple ROI companies and hospitals as defendants and demand
reimbursement for prior charges as well as for prospective pricing adjustments.
The Company is currently a party to several such suits in various stages of
development. One such suit styled <i><font style="font-style:italic;">McShane v.
Recordex Acquisition Corp.&nbsp;&amp; Sourcecorp, Incorporated</font></i>,
filed in the Court of Common Pleas Philadelphia County,&nbsp;Pennsylvania,
alleges among other things that the Company intentionally charges more for
providing copies of medical records than is permitted under Pennsylvania law. In
September&nbsp;2004, the court entered its order certifying a class in this
matter.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Spohr. et. al. v.
F.Y.I. Incorporated, et. al.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2000, the
Company filed an action styled <i><font style="font-style:italic;">F.Y.I.
Incorporated v. Spohr, et. al.</font></i> in Dallas, Texas, in which it
asserted claims for breach of contract, fraud, and negligent misrepresentation
against the sellers of two related companies the Company acquired in December&nbsp;1998
(the &#147;Texas Action&#148;). The Texas Action was later removed to federal court and
ultimately dismissed on jurisdictional grounds. The Company reasserted these
claims in two actions that were later consolidated; one styled <i><font style="font-style:italic;">F.Y.I. Incorporated v. Spohr, et. al.</font></i> in
Superior Court of the State of California in the County of Sacramento, Case No.&nbsp;01-AS-00721
(the &#147;Sacramento Action&#148;) and one styled <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Spohr,
et. al. v. F.Y.I. Incorporated, et. al.</font></i> in the Superior Court of the
State of California in the County of San Francisco, Case No.&nbsp;318703 (the &#147;San
Francisco Action&#148;). In the consolidated action, the Company additionally filed
claims against the sellers&#146; accountants and the two sellers filed claims
against the Company; however, in February&nbsp;2004, the judge in the
Sacramento Action dismissed the Company&#146;s claims against the sellers&#146;
accountants. The sellers allege that the Company&#146;s former subsidiary wrongfully
failed and refused to execute and deliver a requested estoppel certificate, and
that the failure to provide such estoppel certificate harmed the landlord in
that they were allegedly denied favorable terms on a refinancing of the
property and were allegedly prevented from completing a timely sale of the
property. Sellers alleged damages of approximately $1.5&nbsp;million. The
Company asserted damages in excess of $8&nbsp;million. On February&nbsp;3,&nbsp;2005,
the parties settled this matter on mutually acceptable terms consistent with
previous amounts accrued.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Contract-related Contingencies</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has certain
contingent liabilities that arise in the ordinary course of providing services
to its customers. These contingencies are generally the result of contracts
that require the Company to comply with certain performance measurements or the
delivery of certain services by a specified deadline. The Company believes that
the ultimate liability, if any, incurred under these contract provisions will
not have a material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial
condition, results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Concentration of Credit Risk</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial instruments that
potentially subject the Company to concentration of credit risk consist
primarily of cash and cash equivalents and trade receivables. The Company
maintains cash and cash equivalents and certain other financial instruments at
various major financial institutions across many geographic areas. Credit risk
on trade receivables is minimized as a result of the large number of entities
comprising our client base and their dispersion across many industries and
geographic areas.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a18_SubsequentEvents_115313"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">18. Subsequent Events</font></b></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Discontinued
Operations</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the first quarter
of 2005, the Company formally committed to a plan of divestiture for a
non-strategic asset group related to its litigation service operations reported
in the Healthcare, Regulatory and Legal Compliance segment in prior periods. During
2004, the operation contributed approximately $3.7 million of revenue and loss
before income taxes of approximately $0.3 million. The Company has concluded
the asset group meets the requirements for discontinued operations accounting
treatment as outlined in SFAS No. 144, &#147;<i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting
for the Impairment or Disposal of Long-Lived Assets</font></i>&#148; subsequent to
December&nbsp;31, 2004. As such, the results associated with this litigation
service operation will be accounted for as discontinued operations beginning in
the first quarter of 2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a19_SegmentReporting_115313"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">19. Segment Reporting</font></b></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company aggregates its service offerings and
operations into two reportable segments: (i)&nbsp;Information Management and
Distribution, and (ii)&nbsp;Healthcare, Regulatory, and Legal Compliance. The
Company&#146;s reportable segments are organized around customer types and service
offerings possessing similar economic characteristics. Management evaluates
segment performance based on revenue and income before income taxes. All
centrally incurred corporate costs are allocated to the segments based
principally on operating income of the reportable segments measured before the
inclusion of the expense related to the contingent consideration overpayments
discussed in Note 3. The reporting segments follow the same accounting policies
used for the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements as described in the
summary of significant accounting policies.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The identified segments are as follows:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Information Management and
Distribution.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></b>This segment offers Business Process
Outsourcing (&#147;BPO&#148;) solutions that help its customers manage the <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Document In-flow</font></i>, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Workflow Processing</font></i> and <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Statement Out-flow</font></i> of their mission
critical business document processes. This segment&#146;s BPO solutions enable customers
to automate their complex workflow processes by digitizing extremely large
volumes of documents, capturing information from the documents, hosting
electronic documents on the Company&#146;s Web-based repository, and preparing
statements that customers mail or present electronically to their end users. In
2004, Information Management and Distribution represented 50.5% of revenue.
During 2004, revenue in the Information Management and Distribution segment
consisted of approximately $174.1&nbsp;million of recurring revenue and
approximately $20.4&nbsp;million of project revenue.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Healthcare, Regulatory, and Legal
Compliance.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></b>This segment offers specialized knowledge-based
processing and consulting services that include medical records release
services, record management </p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">79</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SOURCECORP, INCORPORATED AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">19.
Segment Reporting</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">services for healthcare
institutions, temporary staffing for healthcare institutions, providing managed
care payment compliance reviews, class action claims administration services,
and professional economic research and litigation services. In 2004,
Healthcare, Regulatory, and Legal Compliance represented 49.5% of revenue.
During 2004, revenue in the Healthcare, Regulatory and Legal Compliance segment
consisted of approximately $113.4&nbsp;million of project revenue and
approximately $77.4&nbsp;million of recurring revenue.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company measures segment profit as income from
continuing operations before taxes. Information on the segments follows (in
thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, the
Company realigned certain operations in order to leverage management expertise,
reduce costs, maximize profitability and better align these operations with
other operating units of similar core competencies. The realignment resulted in
certain operations being </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">80</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SOURCECORP, INCORPORATED AND SUBSIDIARIES<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">19.
Segment Reporting (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">transferred from the
Information Management and Distribution reportable segment to the Healthcare,
Regulatory, and Legal Compliance reportable segment. The Company has
reclassified prior period amounts to be consistent with the current year
segment reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2002, 2003 and 2004, capital expenditures were approximately $7.8&nbsp;million,
$13.6&nbsp;million and $13.8&nbsp;million, respectively, in the Information
Management and Distribution segment and approximately $2.7&nbsp;million,
$2.8&nbsp;million and $3.3&nbsp;million, respectively, in the Healthcare,
Regulatory, and Legal Compliance segment.</font></p>

<div>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="item9"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 9.</font></b></a><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and
Financial Disclosure</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="item9a"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 9A.</font></b></a><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Controls and
Procedures</font></i></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a)&nbsp;Evaluation of disclosure controls and
procedures.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company maintains disclosure controls and procedures, which it has designed to
ensure that material information related to the Company, including its
consolidated subsidiaries, is made known to a group comprised of designated
members of the Company&#146;s senior management, designated members of functional
divisions of the Company, and/or the certifying officers (i.e. Chief Executive
Officer and Chief Financial Officer) (collectively, the &#147;Disclosure Committee&#148;),
on a timely basis, and that information required to be disclosed in reports it
files under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 is recorded, processed,
summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#146;s rules
and forms. As of December&nbsp;31, 2004, the Company carried out an evaluation,
under the supervision and with the participation of the Company&#146;s management,
including the Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, of
the effectiveness of the design and operation of the Company&#146;s disclosure
controls and procedures pursuant to Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as
amended, Rule&nbsp;13a-15 and 15d-15. Based upon that evaluation,
the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that the
Company&#146;s disclosure controls and procedures are effective in timely alerting
them to material information relating to the Company (including its
consolidated subsidiaries) required to be included in the Company&#146;s periodic
SEC filings. Because of the inherent limitations of disclosure controls,
including the possibility of collusion or improper management override of
controls, no matter how comprehensive or well designed such controls are,
management may not in all cases be alerted to material information relating to
the Company (including its consolidated subsidiaries) required to be included
in the Company&#146;s periodic SEC filings.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b)&nbsp;Changes in internal controls</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In light of the events
giving rise to the Company&#146;s restatement, more fully described in Item 7, Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis
of Financial Condition and Results of Operations and in Note 3 to the
consolidated financial statements, the Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer and
Chief Financial Officer have made changes in internal control over financial
reporting in order to address the causes of the restatement.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s
investigation of the circumstances giving rise to the accounting errors that
were corrected in the restatement&nbsp;identified the following issues, which
collectively were a material weakness in our internal control over financial
reporting that were found to have existed through September&nbsp;30, 2004:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Certain employees of the
Operating Subsidiary responsible for the internal control processes at the
Operating Subsidiary either colluded with or coerced individuals to override
the internal controls related to the following processes:</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Billing and
revenue recognition.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Contractual
compliance.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Change
management controls over the IT environment, specifically with regard to
software programs designed to calculate customer invoicing and revenue
recognition.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Monitoring
of non-system generated journal entries of the Operating Subsidiary that were
recorded by those individuals involved in the activities mentioned above.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">82</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='82',FILE='C:\JMS\dschwar\05-2358-2\task380768\2358-2-ga.htm',USER='dschwar',CD='Mar 31 14:10 2005' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company took the following actions to correct the underlying material
weaknesses giving rise to the restatement:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Terminated
certain individuals involved in overriding the internal controls at the
Operating Subsidiary and replace them with new management.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Performed
a review and made improvements to the production and revenue accounting systems
affecting our revenue accounting and customer invoicing at the Operating
Subsidiary.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Further
segregated internal control responsibilities of the Operating Subsidiary
through the centralization of accounting related functions into the Company&#146;s
corporate accounting department.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Established
additional monitoring controls and procedures regarding compliance with the
Company&#146;s customer arrangements.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Increased
Internal Audit&#146;s company-wide testing of internal controls related to customer
invoicing and revenue recognition to help ensure the internal controls are
operating as designed.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 30.0pt;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Performed
additional contract review procedures as an interim step to adding a
company-wide contract compliance function.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The changes to internal
control over financial reporting described above were either implemented in the
fourth quarter of 2004, or in the case of the addition of a company-wide
contract compliance function, is in the process of being implemented. In
addition, during the fourth quarter, the Company augmented its documentation of
certain policies, procedures and processes and modified certain process level
controls. Except as described above, there has been no significant change in
our internal control over financial reporting during the fourth quarter which
materially affected, or is reasonably likely to affect, our internal control
over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under Section 404 of the
Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, we are required to include in this Annual Report on
Form 10-K (i) a report from our management regarding the Company&#146;s internal
controls over financial reporting, which report is required to include, among
other things, an assessment and statement as to the effectiveness of our
internal controls over financial reporting as of December 31, 2004 and (ii) an
attestation report of our independent registered public accounting firm on
management&#146;s assessment of such internal controls.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November 30, 2004, the
SEC issued an exemptive order (SEC Release No. 50754) which provides a 45-day
extension for the filing of the management report and the related attestation
report by eligible companies. We have elected to rely on this 45-day extension,
and therefore, this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K does not include such
reports. We intend to include such reports in an amendment to this Annual
Report on Form 10-K in accordance with the SEC&#146;s exemptive order.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2004, we spent
considerable time and internal and external resources analyzing, documenting
and testing our system of internal controls over financing reporting and have
substantially completed our internal evaluation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There can be no assurance,
however, that one or more material weaknesses in our internal controls over
financial reporting will not be identified during the 45-day extension period,
that management will be able to assert that our internal controls over
financial reporting are effective as of December 31, 2004 or that our
independent registered public accounting firm will be able to attest that
management&#146;s report is fairly stated or express an unqualified opinion on the
effectiveness of our internal controls. If such weaknesses are identified or if
our independent registered public accounting firm does not render an
unqualified attestation, it could result in a loss of investor confidence in
our financial reports, adversely affect our stock price and/or subject us to
sanctions or investigation by regulatory authorities.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="item9b"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 9B.</font></b></a><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Other
Information</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>
